note: What every pinned artifact in this crate actually is. `placeholder` means the file was generated in this repository and matches nothing real; `vendor-published` means it came from the vendor that signs it; `captured` means it was read off our own hardware; `empty-refuses-all` is a reference set with no entries, which anchors nothing and refuses everything. A placeholder so evidence from genuine hardware fails closed against it. The trust ceiling in prism_protocol::MAX_VERIFIABLE_TRUST_CLASS may not sit above a rung whose artifacts are still placeholders, and tests in this crate fail the build if it does. The confidential rung adds no new pinned file: it reuses roots/nvidia-device-identity-root.der and reference/h100-measurements.json (both listed at isolated) and reads the confidential-mode flag from the report itself. Its real-evidence proof is the checked-in genuine NVIDIA CC vector under tests/fixtures/nvidia-cc/genuine, a single-GPU H100 CC report captured from confidential silicon whose signature chains to the root above and whose feature flag names a single-GPU confidential mode.

artifacts.subject: CN=NVIDIA Device Identity CA, O=NVIDIA
artifacts.caveat: Taken from NVIDIA's own verifier repository rather than from an NVIDIA PKI endpoint. Confirm against a second NVIDIA-published copy before treating the pin as authoritative.

Golden digests NVIDIA publishes for this driver, not values read off our own card, so they say what an H100 running this driver should report. The RIM is an XML-signed document and this verifier does not check that signature yet, so their integrity rests on the transport.

production_computation.method: Independently verify the official release manifest and measurement.tdx.cbor, recompute ACPI hashes from the exact public VmConfig, and call tdx_measurements_from_measurement_document. The four expected registers are derived before comparing to the live node's diagnostic Info.
production_computation.caveat: Matching diagnostic Info is not Intel-signed evidence acceptance. Runtime verification still requires Intel-valid quote/collateral, strict TCB/debug policy, the complete pinned tuple, runtime replay, boot identities, and scope-bound report data.
